en.title: Looking for a job
en.summary: Reading an advertisement, writing a CV and a covering letter, and asking for help.

paragraphs: Finding a job takes several steps: you read the advertisement, prepare a CV, write a letter and apply. In this lesson you will practise the language of each step and learn two useful tenses for talking about your experience.
Ellie has finished university and visits a careers adviser in Leeds.

lines.speaker: Ellie
lines.text: I'm looking for a job in marketing. Where should I start?

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: First, update your CV. Then check the vacancies on the main job websites.

lines.speaker: Ellie
lines.text: Do I need a covering letter?

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Yes, send one with every application. Say why you want the job and what you can offer.

lines.speaker: Ellie
lines.text: I've applied for three jobs already, but I haven't heard anything yet.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Don't worry. Employers often take two or three weeks to reply.

lines.speaker: Ellie
lines.text: Should I ring them to ask?

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Wait a week, then send a short, polite e-mail.

paragraphs: **1. The present perfect links the past and the present.** Use have or has plus the past participle for an action with a result now, often with already, yet and just. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
WordPositionExample
alreadybefore the participleI've already applied for three jobs.
yetend of questions and negativesHave you heard anything yet?
justbefore the participleI have just sent my CV.
ever / neverbefore the participleI have never worked abroad.

paragraphs: **2. Should gives advice.** Should + base verb says what is best to do; it is softer than must. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
FunctionExample
adviceYou should update your CV.
negative adviceYou shouldn't send it without a letter.
questionShould I attach a photo?
strongerYou must check the closing date.

items: A CV (curriculum vitae) is called a resume in the United States.
A vacancy is a job that is available, and an applicant is a person who applies.
References are people who can speak about your work.
Experience is uncountable: I have a lot of experience.

paragraphs: Employers in Britain expect a short, clear CV of one or two pages and a covering letter written for that particular job, not a general one. Many applications are made online.
